entry: Dance music genre and subculture. Disco emerged in the late 1960s from the urban nightlife scene of the [[United States]], with a sound typified by four-on-the-floor beats, syncopated basslines, string sections, brass and horns, electric pianos, [[Synthesizer|synthesizers]], and electric rhythm guitars. DJs mixed records at clubs such as Studio 54 in [[Manhattan]], and films such as *Saturday Night Fever* (1977) and *Thank God It's Friday* (1978) contributed to its mainstream popularity. Disco declined sharply in the United States after Disco Demolition Night on July 12, 1979, but it remained popular in Italy and some European countries and spread to [[India]] and the [[Middle East]], where it was blended with regional folk styles. It was a key influence on [[Electronic dance music|electronic dance music]], [[Hip-hop]], new wave, and post-disco, and it has had several revivals since the 1990s.

American instant messaging and VoIP social platform, conceived by Jason Citron and Stanislav Vishnevskiy. It was publicly released in May 2015 and allows voice calls, video calls, [[Text messaging|text messaging]], and media, privately or in communities called "servers." It became widely used by [[Esports|esports]] and LAN tournament gamers. The platform runs on Windows, [[MacOS|macOS]], [[Android (operating system)|Android]], [[IOS|iOS]], Linux, and in [[Web browser|web browsers]]. As of 2025, it had 200 million monthly active users.

Philosophical and autobiographical treatise by [[René Descartes|Descartes]], published in 1637. It is best known as the source of the phrase *Je pense, donc je suis* ("I think, therefore I am"), which appears in Part IV. Descartes tackled the problem of [[Skepticism|skepticism]] by starting from doubt of everything, so as to assess the world from a fresh perspective free of preconceived notions. The work is important to the development of modern philosophy and the natural sciences. Written in French to reach a wider audience than Latin would have allowed, it was originally published in Leiden, Netherlands, and a Latin translation appeared in 1656 in [[Amsterdam]]. It was intended as an introduction to three works, *La Dioptrique*, *Les Météores*, and *La Géométrie*, the last containing concepts that later developed into the [[Cartesian coordinate system]]. With *Meditations on First Philosophy*, *Principles of Philosophy*, and *Rules for the Direction of the Mind*, it forms the base of the [[Epistemology|epistemology]] known as Cartesianism.

[[Probability distribution]] over a finite set of outcomes that are all equally likely, each with probability 1/n for n outcomes. It is a symmetric distribution studied in [[Probability theory|probability theory]] and [[Statistics|statistics]]. A fair six-sided [[Dice|die]] is a common example, with each face having probability 1/6, although the distribution of the sum of two dice rolls is not uniform. Such distributions can be defined over any finite set, including random [[Permutation|permutations]]. When the outcomes are the [[Integer|integers]] in an interval [a,b], a and b are the distribution's parameters and n = b − a + 1. Estimating the maximum of such a distribution from a sample is known as the German tank problem, after Allied forces used it in [[World War II]] to estimate German tank production.

[[Track and field]] event in which athletes throw a heavy disc, or discus, as far as possible. The event originated in ancient Greece, where it was one of the events of the ancient Greek pentathlon, and it is part of the modern [[Decathlon|decathlon]]. It was revived in Magdeburg, Germany, in the 1870s and has been part of the modern [[Summer Olympic Games]] since the 1896 Summer Olympics. Women's competition, begun in the early 20th century, was added to the Olympic program for the 1928 Games. František Janda-Suk of [[Bohemia]] (now the [[Czech Republic]]) introduced the rotational throw after studying the statue Discobolus and won a silver medal at the 1900 Olympics. The rules are virtually identical to those of [[Shot put|shot put]], except that the circle is larger.

Series of fantasy comedy novels, graphic novels, and associated works by English author Terry Pratchett, set on a flat planet balanced on four elephants that stand on a giant turtle. The series consists of 41 novels, from *The Colour of Magic* (1983) to *The Shepherd's Crown* (2015), published posthumously. The novels satirize [[Fantasy|fantasy]] conventions, [[Myth|mythology]], and [[Folklore|folklore]], and comment on contemporary cultural, political, and scientific issues. More than 80 million Discworld books have been sold in 37 languages, and four novels were in the top 100 of the [[BBC]] Big Read.

[[Emotion|Emotional]] response of rejection or revulsion to something potentially contagious or offensive. Disgust is experienced primarily in relation to [[Taste|taste]], and secondarily to anything that causes a similar feeling by [[Sense of smell|smell]], touch, or vision. It is one of the basic emotions in Robert Plutchik's theory and invokes a characteristic facial expression. Unlike fear, anger, and sadness, it is associated with a decrease in heart rate and with proto-nausea of the stomach. It is believed to have evolved to help avoid [[Pathogen|pathogens]], with common elicitors including [[Feces|feces]], spoiled food, and dead bodies. Research has found a relationship between disgust and [[Anxiety disorder|anxiety disorders]], including contamination-related [[Obsessive–compulsive disorder|obsessive–compulsive disorder]].

Machine that cleans [[Tableware|dishware]], cookware, and [[Cutlery|cutlery]] automatically. Unlike manual dishwashing, which relies on physical scrubbing, it sprays hot water, typically between 45 and 75 °C (110 and 170 °F), mixed with detergent from rotating sprayers, and recirculates the mixture to save water and energy. A rinse aid reduces water spots, and the dishes are then dried by one of several methods. Industrial dishwashers in hotels and restaurants wash at 65–71 °C (149–160 °F) and sanitize with a booster heater that provides an 82 °C (180 °F) "final rinse" or with a chemical sanitizer. The most successful early hand-powered model was invented in 1886 by Josephine Cochrane, whose design was unveiled at the 1893 World's Fair in [[Chicago]]. Dishwashers were sold as domestic utilities from the postwar boom of the 1950s, albeit only to the wealthy.

American children's pay television channel and flagship property of Disney Kids & Family, a unit of [[The Walt Disney Company]]. Launched on April 18, 1983, as a premium channel, it dropped "The" from its name in 1997 and shifted its focus to children and adolescents ages 6–14. As of November 2023, it was available to approximately 70 million pay television households in the [[United States]], down from a peak of 100 million in 2011, amid competition from Disney+ and from [[Streaming media|streaming media]] and [[Social media|social media]] platforms.

[[Amusement park|Theme park]] at the Disneyland Resort in [[Anaheim, California]], United States, opened on July 17, 1955. It was the first theme park opened by [[The Walt Disney Company|the Walt Disney Company]] and the only one designed under the direct supervision of [[Walt Disney]]. The park pioneered a strict dedication to theming and cleanliness, a berm to block views of the outside world, and a hub-and-spoke layout, features that influenced theme park design. Later additions include New Orleans Square (1966), Bear Country (1972, now Bayou Country), Mickey's Toontown (1993), and [[Star Wars|Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge]] (2019). With 757 million visits as of December 2021, it has had a larger cumulative attendance than any other theme park. It received 17.406 million visitors in 2025, the second most visited amusement park in the world that year, behind Magic Kingdom.

Mixture in which particles of one material are distributed through a continuous [[Phase (matter)|phase]] of another material, which may be in the same or different states of matter. Dispersions are classified by particle size, whether precipitation occurs, and the presence of Brownian motion. Dispersions of particles large enough to settle are called [[Suspension (chemistry)|suspensions]], while those of smaller particles are [[Colloid|colloids]] and solutions. Common types include [[Emulsion|emulsions]], [[Foam|foams]], [[Gel|gels]], and aerosols. Dispersion occurs through [[Diffusion|diffusion]] and [[Convection|convection]], with convection dominant in significant turbulent flow and diffusion dominant where there is little to no turbulence. Some liquid dispersions become gels, or even solids, at a concentration of the dispersed phase above a critical level that depends on particle size and interfacial tension.

Digital display interface developed by the Video Electronics Standards Association (VESA) to connect a video source, such as a computer, to a display such as a monitor. It can carry digital audio and other data, such as [[USB]], over one cable, using packet-based transmission similar to that of [[Ethernet]]. Adapters are available for connecting it to [[HDMI]], DVI, and VGA. Some implementations support Consumer Electronics Control, which allows devices to be operated with a single [[Remote control|remote control]].

Dismemberment of a deceased animal or plant body to study its [[Anatomy|anatomical]] structure, from [[Latin]] *dissecare* ("to cut to pieces"). Less extensive dissection of plants and small animals preserved in [[Formaldehyde|formaldehyde]] solution is common in [[Biology|biology]] classes, while medical students carry out extensive dissections of cadavers as part of their teaching in anatomy, [[Pathology|pathology]], and forensic medicine. An [[Autopsy|autopsy]] uses dissection to determine the cause of death in humans. In [[Surgery|surgery]], dissection means separating an organ, nerve, or blood vessel from its surrounding [[Connective tissue|connective tissue]] to minimize unwanted damage. Objections to the use of cadavers have led to alternatives such as virtual dissection of computer models.

Dissociative disorder, previously known as multiple personality disorder, characterized by at least two personality states, or "alters." The diagnosis is controversial. The trauma model views it as an organic response to severe childhood trauma, while the sociogenic model treats it as learned behavior shaped by [[Therapy|therapy]], culture, and [[Mass media|media]]. After multiple personality disorder was recognized in DSM-III in 1975, diagnoses reached 50,000 by the 1990s, before a sharp decline and reclassification as dissociative identity disorder in DSM-IV. Treatment generally involves supportive care and [[Psychotherapy|psychotherapy]].

Breakup of the [[Soviet Union]] into independent sovereign states, formally completed on December 26, 1991. Unrest in the 15 union republics became political conflict with the central government: [[Estonia]] declared state sovereignty on November 16, 1988, and [[Lithuania]] declared independence in March 1990. An August 1991 coup attempt by communist hardliners against [[Mikhail Gorbachev]] failed, and the turmoil caused the central government in Moscow to lose influence, so many republics declared independence. On December 8, 1991, the leaders of the three founding republics signed the Belovezha Accords, which established the [[Commonwealth of Independent States]]. On December 25, Gorbachev resigned and transferred his presidential powers to [[Boris Yeltsin]]. The dissolution marked the end of the [[Cold War]] and the culmination of the [[Revolutions of 1989]].

Numerical or occasionally qualitative measure of how far apart objects, points, people, or ideas are. In [[Physics|physics]] and everyday usage, distance may refer to a physical [[Length|length]] or to an estimate based on other criteria. The straight-line, or [[Euclidean geometry|Euclidean]], distance between two points is the usual meaning in classical physics and is computed with the [[Pythagorean theorem]]. The shortest path along the curved surface of the [[Earth]] is approximated by the great-circle distance on a sphere, and is known as a geodesic. In [[Theory of relativity|relativity]], distances depend on the choice of inertial frame of reference, and on galactic scales the [[Expansion of the universe]] also affects measurement. Many abstract notions of distance are formalized in mathematics as a [[Metric space]].

Process of separating the components of a liquid [[Mixture|mixture]] by selective boiling and condensation of the vapors in a still. It operates at pressures from 0.14 [[Bar (unit)|bar]] to nearly 21 bar, and can separate components whose relative volatilities range from 1.17 to 81.2. Its uses include producing alcoholic beverages from fermented products, [[Desalination|desalination]] for potable water, and fractional distillation in [[Oil refinery|oil refineries]]. Cryogenic air separation yields [[Oxygen|oxygen]], [[Nitrogen|nitrogen]], and [[Argon|argon]] for industrial gases. Distillation has an enormous environmental footprint, consuming approximately 25% of all industrial energy use. Akkadian tablets dated c. 1200 BC describe perfumery operations and provide evidence that an early form of distillation was known to the Babylonians of ancient [[Mesopotamia]].

Property of two mathematical operations, most commonly [[Multiplication|multiplication]] over [[Addition|addition]]. The distributive law, x⋅(y+z) = x⋅y + x⋅z, holds in elementary algebra; for example, 2⋅(1+3) = (2⋅1) + (2⋅3). It is part of the definition of most algebraic structures with two operations, including [[Complex number|complex numbers]], polynomials, matrices, [[Ring (mathematics)|rings]], and [[Field (mathematics)|fields]]. It also appears in [[Boolean algebra]] and [[Mathematical logic|mathematical logic]], where each of the logical and (∧) and or (∨) distributes over the other. In rings and fields, multiplication is distributive over addition, but addition is not distributive over multiplication.

American vedette, [[Burlesque|burlesque]] dancer, model, and businesswoman. She is credited with re-popularizing burlesque performance and was dubbed the "Queen of Burlesque." She has appeared in [[CSI: Crime Scene Investigation]] and RuPaul's Drag Race, and has released two books on burlesque history, fetishism, and beauty. She toured the world with her shows in cities including [[Paris]], London, Berlin, and New York. She has also created four perfumes and her own lingerie brand. She was married to singer Marilyn Manson from December 2005 to January 2007, and performed in his music videos.

Collection of lyric poems in [[Persian language|Persian]] by the Sufi mystic [[Rumi]], containing more than 40,000 verses and over 3,000 [[Ghazal|ghazals]]. Also known as *Divan-i Kabir* and *Divan-i Shams*, it is dedicated to Rumi's spiritual teacher, Shams-i Tabrizi, and contains many verses praising him and lamenting his disappearance. Shams left Konya in 1246, returned, and vanished again in 1248, possibly having been murdered. Most of the poems were written in the aftermath of this second disappearance, and they were collected by Rumi's students after his death. Rumi's trance-like style differs from that of other Islamic poets, and some poems are in [[Arabic]]. By the sixteenth century, editors arranged the poems alphabetically by the last letter of each line, a method still used in modern Iranian editions.

Gastrointestinal disease characterized by inflammation of diverticula, abnormal pouches that develop in the wall of the [[Large intestine|large intestine]]. Symptoms typically include sudden lower abdominal pain, sometimes with [[Diarrhea|diarrhea]]. Risk factors include [[Obesity|obesity]], [[Smoking|smoking]], and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs. Diagnosis is typically by [[CT scan]], and mild cases are treated with antibiotics by mouth and a liquid diet. The disease is common in the [[Western world]], where about 35% of people have diverticulosis, the presence of uninflamed pouches.

Attempt to gain insight into a question or situation by way of a [[Ritual|ritual]] or practice of [[Magic (supernatural)|magic]]. Diviners read signs, events, or omens, often claiming insight from spirits, gods, or the "will of the universe." Practices include [[Astrology|astrology]], [[Tarot|tarot]] card reading, rune casting, and tea-leaf reading. Where a distinction from fortune-telling is drawn, divination is more formal, ritualistic, and social, usually in a religious context. Rigorous experiments do not support the notion that divination can predict the future more reliably than would be possible without such techniques, and it has been dismissed as [[Superstition|superstition]] in the modern era. In antiquity, [[Cicero]] criticized it in *De Divinatione* (1st century BC). The Oracle of [[Amun]] at Siwa was visited by [[Alexander the Great]] in 332 BC.

Italian narrative poem by [[Dante Alighieri|Dante]], begun c. 1308 and completed c. 1321, shortly before the author's death. Widely considered the pre-eminent work of [[Italian literature]] and one of the greatest works of Western literature, it describes Dante's journey through [[Hell]], [[Purgatory]], and Paradise, in which souls receive punishment or reward based on their actions. Allegorically, it represents the soul's journey toward [[God]]. Dante is guided by [[Virgil]] through Hell and most of Purgatory, and by Beatrice through Paradise. Written in Tuscan, it helped establish the standardized Italian language. Its 14,233 lines are divided into three cantiche, [[Inferno (Dante)|Inferno]], Purgatorio, and Paradiso, of 33 cantos each, plus an introductory canto.

Sport of jumping or falling into water from a platform or springboard, usually while performing [[Acrobatics|acrobatics]]. Diving is an internationally recognized sport and part of the [[Olympic Games]], and it is also a recreational pastime. Competitors share strength, flexibility, and air awareness with [[Dance|dancers]] and gymnasts. The first modern diving competitions were held in [[England]] in the 1880s, and the sport likely derives from diving at the start of [[Swimming|swimming]] races. Fancy diving developed from gymnastic traditions in [[Germany]] and [[Sweden]], and plain and fancy diving were combined into one Olympic event, highboard diving, in 1928. Women were first allowed to compete for the 1912 Olympics. Dmitri Sautin holds the record for most Olympic diving medals, with eight between 1992 and 2008.

One of the four basic operations of [[Arithmetic|arithmetic]], alongside [[Addition|addition]], [[Subtraction|subtraction]], and [[Multiplication|multiplication]]. The number being divided is the dividend, the number dividing it is the divisor, and the result is the quotient. Division of natural numbers may leave a remainder: if 21 apples are divided between four people, everyone receives five apples and one apple remains. Extending the numbers to [[Rational number|rational]] or [[Real number|real numbers]] makes division the inverse of multiplication, so a = c / b means a × b = c, but division by zero is not defined. Division is not commutative or associative: (24 / 6) / 2 = 2, while 24 / (6 / 2) = 8. Division also appears in algebraic structures such as [[Field (mathematics)|fields]], where division by every nonzero element is defined, and in Euclidean domains, where a Euclidean division with remainder is defined.
